title: Material incidents and insurance
summary: Proposed roadmap for significant-harm reporting, response, evidence handling, coverage verification and a possible future insurance institution. These Goals describe future scope and open decisions, not adopted obligations or active services. Assignment assurance currently supports nonfinancial service undertakings; no operational incident service or verified insurance is established. Milestone steps remain undefined.

goals.title: Define incident reporting and materiality decisions
goals.description: Proposed scope: make possible significant harm reportable and define when a notice qualifies for a material incident procedure. Decide the threshold, who receives and assesses notices, handling under uncertainty, response times and a challenge route. Define required incident notice separately from transport delivery, reading, acknowledgment and consent; reconcile it with Identity's silent clock-out/sign-out policy without resuming sensing or treating silence as consent or fault. Preserve honest and mistaken reporting; an unconfirmed report alone would not establish fabrication, fault, liability or coverage. Material incident remains a provisional term. Hero 7 defines incident requirements; Assignments and participant experience defines the participant handoffs, APK buildout supplies phone presentation, Durable infrastructure defines notice delivery and acceptance semantics, and Server side services supplies the agreed persistent records.

goals.title: Define immediate response and external assistance
goals.description: Proposed scope: specify Non Verba's role in supporting immediate safety, evidence preservation and appropriate medical, police, regulatory, insurance or legal channels for significant harm around Assignments. The procedure must keep urgent assistance and evidence preservation available without awaiting a platform form or final materiality classification. Decide service responsibilities, contacts, availability, handoffs and accountability before making response promises. Server side services owns technical outage and security-event operations; Governance and launch readiness owns provider accountability and actual institutional adoption. Where a technical event also involves Assignment harm, cross-reference the relevant domain records. The project has no operational incident service; signed nonfinancial undertakings do not establish staffing or delivery, and adopting institutional duties would not itself authorize a participant's contractual settlement or payment.

goals.title: Preserve incident evidence and define scoped disclosure
goals.description: Proposed scope: specify incident preservation and recipient-specific disclosure requirements using the shared case and scrutiny projection defined with Dispute procedure and settlement. Retain original sensor and Assignment records with their original request and policy context, distinguish later attributed additions and preserve explicit missing, unsigned and failed-attempt states. Sensors owns acquisition formats and evidence semantics; these records alone establish neither physical truth nor fault. Identity owns identity assurance, custody and general access policy; the workflow, service and APK Heroes supply transport, hosted controls and local handling. Decide lawful recipient scope, minimization and retention; scrutiny must not automatically include private registration, identity or authentication media, expose member records, or authorize underwriting reuse. Local exports and journals remain components rather than an operational custody service.

goals.title: Define external coverage requirements and admission checks
goals.description: Proposed scope: investigate whether qualifying existing coverage can support a narrowly selected task class before Assignment formation. Governance and launch readiness selects and reviews pilot scope and jurisdiction; Hero 7 proposes the task-specific protection and qualification requirements and what verification could establish. Examine insured parties, activities, location, period, limits, deductibles and exclusions. A candidate gate would withhold admission when required coverage is absent or unverifiable, without erasing an already formed Contract. Assignments presents the agreed admission and formation handoff; Server side services supplies any authorized provider records and enforcement, and APK buildout implements phone presentation. No gate, status format or verification method is selected; a policy document alone establishes neither event coverage nor safe operations.

goals.title: Coordinate incident and contractual claims
goals.description: Proposed scope: define how one Assignment can retain both a payment dispute and claims involving significant harm. Dispute procedure and settlement owns contractual consequence, consent and exact release or closure scope; Hero 7 owns incident materiality, response, external disclosure and coverage requirements. A payment resolution would identify harm claims left outside its scope. An incident notice, referral, insurer communication or scrutiny export would not itself instruct payment, establish liability or coverage, settle harm claims or authorize closure. Applicable rights and institutional authority remain questions for Governance and launch readiness. No general incident closure or settlement rule is adopted.

goals.title: Research a future insurance institution
goals.description: Proposed scope: develop the owner's stated aim of an insurance institution tied to the Assignment process. Compare a carrier partnership, underwriting technology, delegated insurance functions such as an MGA arrangement, and a separate insurer as alternatives, without assuming an order or selecting a model. Hero 7 supplies research on covered risks, claims and service responsibilities. Governance and launch readiness addresses legal entity and provider accountability, authorization review, formal adoption and the concrete software licensing boundary; Server side services would implement a separately authorized provider interface. No entity, partnership, insurance product or initial launch dependency is established.

goals.title: Assess risk evidence and insurance economics
goals.description: Proposed scope: investigate whether task definitions, qualifications, timelines, evidence, incidents and observed outcomes can support credible risk assessment for a future insurance arrangement. Examine data quality, representative loss information, lawful underwriting reuse and incentives; signatures or rich records alone would not establish actuarial value or accurate physical observations. Hero 7 owns research into insurance-specific pricing, funding, underwriting reserves and surplus options for a defined institutional proposal. Sensors informs observation quality; Governance and launch readiness owns Non Verba's operating economics, legal authority and formal policy adoption. No underwriting dataset, pricing rule, pool, reserve policy or savings promise is established.
